questions.question: Why did large open models move away from full multi-head attention at scale?
options: Full MHA makes optimizers unusable
Full MHA makes the KV cache too large for long-context inference
Full MHA prevents the use of RMSNorm
Full MHA only works on English text
questions.explanation: The lesson emphasizes that long-context serving is often dominated by KV-cache memory rather than raw parameter count. Sharing or compressing K/V heads is how modern models keep inference practical above roughly 13B parameters.

questions.question: What practical advantage does RoPE have over learned absolute position embeddings?
options: RoPE makes training fully deterministic
RoPE eliminates the embedding matrix
RoPE allows context-length extrapolation with scaling tricks instead of stopping at a learned table limit
RoPE removes the need for causal masking
questions.explanation: Learned position embeddings are fixed lookup tables with a hard length limit. RoPE encodes position via deterministic rotations, which lets models stretch farther at inference with techniques like NTK scaling or YaRN.

questions.question: Which list matches the six architectural knobs the lesson says keep changing across 2024-2026 open models?
options: Tokenizer size, optimizer type, dataset mix, learning rate, batch size, checkpoint format
RMSNorm, RoPE, SwiGLU/GeGLU, attention head sharing, dense vs MoE MLP, and pre-norm placement
Beam search, chain-of-thought, RLHF, DPO, quantization, distillation
CUDA version, tensor parallelism, logging, eval harness, API format, prompt template
questions.explanation: The whole point of the lesson is that modern open models are still GPT-like models with a small set of recurring architectural diffs. If you can read those six knobs from config.json, you can usually predict the model's memory and deployment behavior.

questions.question: Llama 3 8B uses 32 query heads and 8 KV heads. What does that imply for KV-cache size versus full MHA?
options: It is about 4x smaller
It is unchanged because queries still have 32 heads
It is about 4x larger
It disappears entirely
questions.explanation: Grouped-query attention shares K and V across groups of query heads. With 32 Q heads and 8 KV heads, the cache stores only one quarter as many K/V streams as full 32-head MHA would.

questions.question: Why can a model like Mixtral 8x7B have far more total parameters than active parameters per token?
options: Because most weights are pruned away at inference time
Because RoPE hides unused parameters from the KV cache
Because the MoE router activates only a small top-k subset of experts for each token
Because RMSNorm merges multiple experts into one
questions.explanation: MoE increases total capacity by storing many experts, but each token only runs through a few of them. That is why Mixtral and DeepSeek can advertise huge total parameter counts while paying compute closer to a much smaller dense model.
